Zer
ZUR
proper noun
Hebrew Tser, perhaps “flint” or “rock”; one of the fenced cities of Naphtali, named once.

Biblical Definition

Zer was one of the fenced (fortified) cities of Naphtali, listed among the strongholds of that tribe: “And the fenced cities are Ziddim, Zer, and Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth” (Josh 19:35). These fenced cities stood along the fair shore of the sea of Chinnereth (Galilee), walled against the enemy. If the name means “flint” or “rock,” it suits a fortress, hard and defensible. The fenced cities of Israel preach both a comfort and a caution. God gave His people walled towns for their safety, that they might dwell secure; the name of the LORD is a strong tower, and the righteous runneth into it and is safe. Yet Israel was warned not to trust in her fenced cities and high walls in the place of the LORD, for the strongest wall is no defence when God withdraws His protection, and the mightiest fortress falls at His word. Zer, a fenced city of Naphtali, reminds the believer that true security is not in the works of men’s hands but in the living God, who is Himself the rock and refuge of His people. Better is trust in the LORD than confidence in walls; the name of the LORD is the only tower that cannot be thrown down.

Webster 1828 Definition

A fenced city of Naphtali, perhaps “flint” (Josh 19:35); a reminder that true security is not in walls but in the LORD, the rock and refuge of His people.

Key Scripture

Josh 19:35 — "And the fenced cities are Ziddim, Zer, and Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth,"

Deu 33:23 — "And of Naphtali he said, O Naphtali, satisfied with favour, and full with the blessing of the LORD: possess thou the west and the south."

Gen 49:21 — "Naphtali is a hind let loose: he giveth goodly words."

Josh 19:39 — "This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Naphtali according to their families, the cities and their villages."

Modern Corruption

A fenced city of Naphtali; it recovers that true security is not in walls but in the LORD, the rock and refuge of His people.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A fenced city named once raises no modern quarrel. Its name, perhaps “flint,” suits a stronghold, and turns the mind to the true rock and refuge of God’s people.

The principle to recover is that security is in the LORD, not in walls. God gave His people fenced cities for safety, yet warned them not to trust in high walls in His place; the strongest fortress falls at His word. The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous runneth into it and is safe. Better is trust in the LORD than confidence in walls; He is the only tower that cannot be thrown down.
